headline: Strait of Hormuz transit ~92% below its pre-disruption norm (sustained)
brief_md:
**Strait of Hormuz** has run at **~6 vessels/day** since around **2026-03-01**, **~92% below** its prior norm of **~75/day** — a level shift sustained for **~91 days**.

_This is a persistent disruption, not a fresh blip. A 28-day rolling baseline has since adapted to the new level, which is why a same-day anomaly detector reads it as 'normal'; it is flagged by comparing today's level to the pre-shift norm._

_Method: sustained level-shift vs pre-disruption norm. Source: IMF PortWatch — daily granularity, refreshed weekly._
source: IMF PortWatch — daily granularity, refreshed weekly

headline: Yucatan Channel avg vessel size 34% above norm — larger ships
brief_md:
**Yucatan Channel** average transiting **vessel size** rose to **~34,567 DWT** on 2026-05-28, **34% above** its 28-day norm of ~25,874 DWT (z = +4.6) — larger ships on average — while the **transit count** stayed near normal (+3%). The count detector can't see this; ship-size is orthogonal to ship-count.

_Average size = transiting capacity (DWT) ÷ vessel count — a fleet-mix shift, **not** capacity utilisation (capacity here is a flow, not a ceiling)._

_Method: STL(7,robust) residual + 28d rolling z. Source: IMF PortWatch — daily granularity, refreshed weekly._
source: IMF PortWatch — daily granularity, refreshed weekly
